title: 「What-焦點句」

omissions: Every numbered Important Rule and Benefit is retained as a separate Chinese-primary card. Where the PDF has no English counterpart, the English explanation is a faithful editorial translation.

formula: What matters is ... / What I mean is ... / What surprised me most was ... / What concerns me is ...

formulas.formula: What matters is + noun phrase / that-clause / whether-clause / wh-clause
What I mean is + that-clause / noun phrase
What surprised me most was + noun phrase / wh-clause
What concerns me is + noun phrase / that-clause / whether-clause / wh-clause

meaning.zh: 本課練習目標句型：What matters is ... / What I mean is ... / What surprised me most was ... / What concerns me is ...。

rules.zh: 雖然這些句子以 What 開始，但它們是陳述句，而不是問句。句末不應使用問號。
rules.en: These are statements, not questions Although these sentences begin with What, they are statements rather than questions. Do not place a question mark at the end. Correct: What matters is whether the information is accurate. Incorrect: What matters is whether the information is accurate?
examples: These are statements, not questions
Although these sentences begin with What, they are statements rather than questions. Do not
place a question mark at the end.
Correct: What matters is whether the information is accurate.
Incorrect: What matters is whether the information is accurate?

rules.zh: 使用正確的連綴動詞：現在概念用 is；固定描述過去反應的 What surprised me most was ... 用 was。
rules.en: Use is with present ideas, but was in the fixed past-reaction frame What surprised me most was ....
examples: Use the correct linking verb
Use is with present ideas:
What matters is ...
What I mean is ...
What concerns me is ...
Use was in the fixed structure describing a past reaction:
What surprised me most was ...

rules.zh: 在 is 或 was 後面，必須接上完整而清晰的重點內容，例如名詞詞組或完整從句。
rules.en: A complete idea must follow is or was The focused information may be: ● a noun phrase: her honesty ● a that-clause: that nobody checked the figures ● a whether-clause: whether the bridge is safe ● a wh-clause: how quickly the children adapted
examples: A complete idea must follow is or was
The focused information may be:
a noun phrase: her honesty
a that-clause: that nobody checked the figures
a whether-clause: whether the bridge is safe
a wh-clause: how quickly the children adapted

rules.zh: 使用 not X, but Y 時，X 和 Y 應盡量採用相同或相近的文法形式。
rules.en: Keep contrasted parts parallel When using not X, but Y, X and Y should have similar grammatical forms. Correct: What matters is not who made the error, but how we will correct it. Correct: What I mean is not that we should cancel the event, but that we should delay it.
examples: Keep contrasted parts parallel
When using not X, but Y, X and Y should have similar grammatical forms.
Correct: What matters is not who made the error, but how we will correct it.
Correct: What I mean is not that we should cancel the event, but that we should delay it.

rules.zh: 按照目的選擇句型：指出重點、澄清意思、突出意外之處或指出憂慮。
rules.en: Choose the What-focus frame according to its purpose: importance, clarification, surprise or concern.
examples: Choose the structure according to its purpose
What matters is ... identifies the most important point.
What I mean is ... clarifies an idea or corrects a misunderstanding.
What surprised me most was ... highlights the most unexpected fact.
What concerns me is ... identifies the speaker’s main worry.

benefits.zh: 這個句型能立即指出句子中最值得留意的重點，讓讀者不會錯過你的主要訊息。 第二句把焦點更明確地放在「準確性」之上。
benefits.en: It directs attention to the key point This structure immediately tells the listener or reader which part of the message deserves the most attention. Compare: Accuracy is more important than speed. What matters is not speed, but accuracy. The second sentence places stronger focus on accuracy.

benefits.zh: 當別人可能誤解你的說話時，你可以使用 What I mean is ... 進一步澄清真正意思。 （我不是說這個計劃毫無用處。我的意思是，它需要更充分的準備。）
benefits.en: It helps you explain yourself clearly You can use What I mean is ... when your first statement may be unclear or misunderstood. Example: I am not saying that the plan is useless. What I mean is that it needs more preparation.

benefits.zh: 這個句型能把主要觀點與背景資料分開，讓讀者清楚知道哪一項才是核心。
benefits.en: It separates the main point from background information Instead of giving several ideas equal importance, the structure shows which idea is central.

benefits.zh: 使用 What surprised me most was ... 和 What concerns me is ...，可以準確指出究竟哪件事 令你感到驚訝或擔心。
benefits.en: It makes reactions and concerns more precise What surprised me most was ... and What concerns me is ... help you identify the exact fact that caused your reaction.

benefits.zh: 這些句型能提供不同的句子開頭，避免重複使用相同表達，使說話、作文、報告及簡報更有變化。
benefits.en: It gives you more sentence variety These structures provide an alternative to repeatedly beginning sentences with: ● The important thing is ... ● I mean ... ● I was surprised by ... ● I am worried about ...
